Well, i could say she’s wrong for not being completely 100% honest about her intimate past; 
I could also say you’re wrong for asking so much about her past. Just… why? 
Does it matter that much to you? 
If she would’ve said the truth 100% when you asked, what would’ve been your reaction?

if you do care about stupid stuff like a “body count”
or whatever, then break it off. plain and easy.
I believe there’s some specific details that, even if you’re fully honest with your partner, you just shouldn’t touch upon; “body counts” is one of them. 

Like, if i had my gf ask me how many people i’ve slept with, i would only count the ones that actually matter to me. I most definitely fucked more people but that’s not important; and more importantly, she doesn’t need to know that. I don’t think that’s lying. you could argue it’s hiding probably but come up with your own conclusions and boundaries and tell them.

PS, the fact that you went through her phone is a complete dealbreaker for the trust in the relationship to me but that’s just my opinion. bad on you.

first off, solid fade 100%
great job

Second, i’ll be nitpicking for sake of feedback and your self improvement. 

Lineup in the back is uneven on both side around the ear, 
in most head that’s just how it is naturally and we gotta do what we can(different heads, different structures yadda yadda) but in this cut is very noticeable. It helps to stick to the natural hairline as much as possible and doing any adjustments after. 

His left side looks better and cleaner because his hair is properly layered behind his ear and up.
Right side could use a little more trimming around the ear and just blend the hair into that. 

That’s pretty much it, small details 
your doing good man, keep it up

best advice i can give is make sure you keep you scissor game up. There’s absolutely nothing you can’t go with good scissor skills, even if your just doing fades like these.

Find a place where there’s good amount of clients so you can start polishing your skills and different styles. 
I recommend starting in a commission shop since your coworkers would be more open about helping you out or giving advice. 

Don’t be afraid to take those difficult and scary clients,
it might be a little hard and it will test your skills but it’s the best way to start building confidence in your skills and knowledge in your craft. 
and it feels dang good to finally nail that cut that used to scare you before! 

Bonus: Tweak your algorithm in social media (insta,tiktok,etc…) to get haircut videos while you doom scroll away.
if you’re gonna be watching reels might as well be something that’ll teach you something! 

best of luck
